q19.

```
ConnectRPC — server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go (plus method wrappers in server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go)
gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON — server/router/api/v1/v1.go
```

**ConnectRPC.** `ConnectServiceHandler.RegisterConnectHandlers` mounts the generated handler on an `http.ServeMux` at line 40 of `connect_handler.go`:

```40:40:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go
		wrap(apiv1connect.NewMemoServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
```

The handler struct embeds `*APIV1Service` (line 21), and the per-RPC adapters that unwrap `connect.Request` and delegate live in `connect_services.go` — that's where `ConnectServiceHandler.CreateMemo` (q11) and `SignIn` (q04) sit.

**gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON.** `v1.go` builds a `runtime.NewServeMux` with auth middleware and registers the same `*APIV1Service` directly against it at line 108:

```108:108:/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go
	if err := v1pb.RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
```

This is what turns the `google.api.http` annotations from q01 and q12 into real routes like `POST /api/v1/memos`.

Both protocols share one implementation: `RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer` takes `s` (the `APIV1Service`) and the Connect handler embeds that same value, so business logic has a single source of truth — the file header comment at lines 17–20 states this explicitly. All eight services from q05 are registered on both paths.
